questions.question: The Resolution of Non-Cooperation movement was confirmed in the annual session of the Indian National Congress at ___________ in December 1920.
questions.solution:
The resolution for the Non-Cooperation Movement was ratified at the Nagpur session of the Congress in December 1920.
  • This session marked a change in the Congress constitution to allow for peaceful, extra-constitutional struggle.
  • C. Vijayaraghavachariar presided over this session.

questions.question: Harshavardhana tried to cross the Narmada to march into the Deccan, but was stopped by a ruler belonging to the Chalukya dynasty, ______.
questions.solution:
Pulakeshin II was the greatest ruler of the Western Chalukyas of Badami who stopped Harsha's expansion.
  • The two kings agreed that the Narmada River would be the boundary between their empires.
  • Pulakeshin II assumed the title Paramesvara after this victory.

questions.question: Battle of Buxar was fought in ______.
questions.solution:
The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764.
  • The combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-daulah, and Shah Alam II were defeated by the British under Hector Munro.
  • This victory led to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), granting the British Diwani rights over Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.

questions.question: Famous ruler Kanishka belonged to the ____________ dynasty.
questions.solution:
Kanishka, the most famous ruler of the Kushana dynasty, reigned in the 2nd century AD.
  • He started the Saka Era in 78 AD.
  • He was a great patron of Mahayana Buddhism and held the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir.

questions.question: Satavahanas was a powerful dynasty in ______ India.
questions.solution:
The Satavahanas were a powerful dynasty in Western and Central India.
  • Their capital was at Paithan (Pratishthana) on the banks of the Godavari.
  • They were famous for issuing coins made of lead.

questions.question: In which of the following places was the Indian Association founded in colonial India?
questions.solution:
The Indian Association was founded in Calcutta in 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose.
  • It was the most important of the pre-Congress nationalist organizations.
  • It focused on creating a strong public opinion on political questions and unifying Indians.

questions.question: In the Tamil region, landless labourers, including slaves, were known as __________ during Sangam age.
questions.solution:
In the Tamil Sangam age, landless labourers were known as kadaisiyar and slaves were called adimai.
  • Vellalar were large landowners.
  • Uzhavar were ordinary ploughmen.

questions.question: Who was responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.solution:
General Dyer was the British officer responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
  • He was later censured by the Hunter Commission but hailed as a hero by some in Britain.
  • He was eventually assassinated by Udham Singh in 1940 (Correction: Dyer died of illness; Udham Singh shot Michael O'Dwyer).

questions.question: Ziyauddin Barani wrote his chronicle’s first version in _____ year.
questions.solution:
Ziyauddin Barani wrote the first version of his chronicle, Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, in 1356.
  • He wrote a second version two years later.
  • His work is a major source of history for the reigns of the Delhi Sultans from Balban to Firoz Shah Tughluq.

questions.question: Battle of Plassey was fought in ______.
questions.solution:
The Battle of Plassey took place in 1757.
  • It was fought between the British East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-daulah.
  • The treachery of Mir Jafar led to the Nawab's defeat.

questions.question: Which of the following city was the capital of the Pandyas?
questions.solution:
Madurai was the capital of the Pandya dynasty.
  • The Pandyas were mentioned by Megasthenes and were known for their pearl fishery.
  • The city was a great center of Tamil Sangam literature.

questions.question: Where was the Communist Party of India (CPI) founded, in 1920?
questions.solution:
The Communist Party of India (CPI) was founded in Tashkent (now in Uzbekistan) in October 1920.
  • Founding members included M.N. Roy, Evelyn Trent, and Abani Mukherji.
  • It was later formally established in India at the Kanpur Conference in 1925.

questions.question: Who was the president of the first session of Congress held in 1885?
questions.solution:
Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee was the president of the first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885.
  • The session was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay.
  • There were 72 delegates present from different parts of India.

questions.question: Which of the following cities emerged as the second capital of the Kushanas during their empire?
questions.solution:
The Kushanas had two major centers of power: Purushpura (Peshawar) and Mathura.
  • Mathura emerged as a major center for art and sculpture (the Mathura School of Art).
  • The Kushanas were among the first to issue gold coins on a large scale in India.

questions.question: In _________, Gandhiji held a Satyagraha at Ahmedabad to solve the dispute between the owners and workers of a cotton mill in the city.
questions.solution:
In 1918, Mahatma Gandhi led a Satyagraha in Ahmedabad for cotton mill workers.
  • The workers were demanding a 35% wage hike.
  • This was the first time Gandhi used 'hunger strike' as a weapon in the Indian struggle.

questions.question: Who among the following found it more difficult to follow the rules of Jainism?
questions.solution:
The rules of Jainism were particularly difficult for peasants to follow.
  • This was because they had to kill insects to protect their crops, which violated the principle of Ahimsa (non-violence).
  • Jainism found more support among traders and artisans.

questions.question: A Khilafat Committee was formed in _____ in March 1919.
questions.solution:
A Khilafat Committee was formed in Delhi in 1919 (Note: Initial committee in March 1919 was in Bombay, but an All India Khilafat Conference was later held in Delhi).
  • The movement protested against the harsh terms imposed on the Ottoman Empire after WWI.
  • It was a major platform for Hindu-Muslim unity.

questions.question: Who among the Mauryan ruler pioneered the propagation of Bauddh Dhamma?
questions.solution:
Ashoka was the first ruler who tried to take his message to the people through inscriptions and propagation of Dhamma.
  • He sent missions to Sri Lanka, Greece, and Central Asia.
  • His son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra went to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism.

questions.question: Savitribai, together with her husband Jyotirao Phule, founded one of India's first girls' schools in Pune, at Bhide Wada in _________.
questions.solution:
Savitribai Phule and her husband founded India's first school for girls at Bhide Wada, Pune, in 1848.
  • She is regarded as the first female teacher of India.
  • She faced great social opposition but continued her work for women's rights and education.

questions.question: In ______, Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat.
questions.solution:
The First Battle of Panipat took place in 1526.
  • Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of Delhi.
  • Babur's use of artillery (cannon) was a decisive factor in his victory, leading to the establishment of the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Whom did Udham Singh assassinate?
questions.solution:
Udham Singh assassinated Michael O'Dwyer in London in 1940.
  • Michael O'Dwyer was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab during the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
  • Udham Singh did this to avenge the victims of the 1919 tragedy.

questions.question: Which of the following Chinese pilgrims visited India about 50 years after Xuan Zang?
questions.solution:
The Chinese monk I-Qing (I-Tsing) visited India in the 7th century, about 50 years after Xuan Zang.
  • He stayed at Nalanda for many years and translated Buddhist texts.
  • He traveled via the sea route through Southeast Asia.

questions.question: In 1986, an operation had to be conducted against terrorists in the Golden Temple. What was the name of this operation?
questions.solution:
Operation Black Thunder was conducted in 1986 (and again in 1988) to flush out militants from the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
  • It followed the earlier Operation Blue Star (1984).
  • The objective was to clear the temple without causing significant damage to the structure.

questions.question: Fa Xian began his journey back from ______.
questions.solution:
Fa Xian (Faxian) began his return journey to China from Bengal (Tamralipti).
  • He was a Chinese Buddhist monk who visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).
  • He focused primarily on collecting Buddhist scriptures.

questions.question: Which of the following books was written by Kautilya?
questions.solution:
Kautilya (also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta) wrote the Arthashastra.
  • It is a classic treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
  • Indica was written by Megasthenes, and Mudra Rakshasa was written by Vishakhadatta.
